title: Job lifecycle
description: Understand job states, expiration, and restart behavior.

sections.title: Four states
table: Accepted and waiting for a worker.
A worker is converting the input.
The output is ready to download.
The attempt failed; inspect the error field.

sections.title: Starting is automatic
paragraphs: POST /v1/jobs uploads and queues in one request. There is no separate start request or created state. Polling may skip queued or running if a small file finishes quickly.

sections.title: Retention and recovery
paragraphs: The default expiry is one hour after creation and is refreshed to one hour after a conversion completes. Use expiresAt from each response as the authoritative deadline. Cleanup runs every minute. Workers have a two-minute conversion timeout.
With CONVRT_DATA_DIR configured, queued and completed jobs survive restarts. Interrupted running jobs become failed with conversion_interrupted. Without persistence, jobs disappear on shutdown.

sections.title: Read the whole response
paragraphs: createdAt records when the server accepted the job. expiresAt tells you when access is expected to expire. A downloadUrl appears only after success, and an error appears after a failed conversion. Status polling does not itself extend retention.

sections.title: Expect state changes between requests
paragraphs: A small file may finish before your first status poll, so your client must accept succeeded immediately. Likewise, a queued job can start just before a delete request reaches the server, producing a 409. Read the current state instead of assuming the last observed state still holds.
A 404 can mean the job expired or was removed, or that the current key is not its owner. Stop polling on 404 and ask the application to resubmit only when a new conversion is intended.
